findings.message: The round 1 P1 on the symlinked SKILL.md is resolved. workflow/skills.py:77-80 dropped the is_symlink() refusal. exists() and is_file() follow the link, so a SKILL.md that is a symlink to a regular file now resolves. _walk and copy_skill copy it as a real file (test_resolve_follows_a_skill_md_symlinked_to_a_regular_file_inside_the_folder). The PRD's own case (PRD line 9: ~/.claude/skills/impeccable is itself a symlink into a shared clone) resolves through the folder's resolve(). A SKILL.md linked outside its resolved skill folder is still refused, as 'SKILL.md resolves outside the skill folder' (test_check_refuses_a_skill_md_symlinked_outside_the_folder). That refusal comes from the design challenge's copy note (challenge.json: 'refuse ... a link that resolves outside the skill folder's resolved root or forms a loop'). It is listed in the RUNBOOK's refusals and names the lane and the skill, so it is a documented, security-motivated boundary: it keeps a skill from copying, for example, a key file into the run directory a worker can read. It does not contradict 'symlinks followed'. Consequence: none blocking. An operator whose SKILL.md points outside its skill folder gets a named refusal at launch and must make the folder itself the symlink.

The [L1](i) canary evidence is now stale against the final argv. [L1](i) asks for one claude --bg canary 'with the skills lane's exact argv'. The canary recorded in docs/handoff/worker-skills.md ('Probes') was run in round 1. Its --settings deny list was a reduced probe list (Read(~/.ssh/**) and an Edit rule on the probe plugin), not the controller's list, and it had no Write rule. Repair 2 then added the Write(/<run>/skills/<lane>/**) deny, and no canary was run again. RUNBOOK 'What loads, what does not' now says so ('round 1's, before the plugin Write deny was added'). The handoff still calls it a canary 'with the exact skills-lane argv'. The risk is low. The codebase's own record (interactive.py:421-424) shows Claude Code accepts a Write(...) rule but never matches it, so the rule should be inert rather than invalidate the settings. The Edit rule already covers Write. Fix: rerun the canary with the final argv (full deny list, both plugin rules), or correct the handoff wording. The [G7] canary-first launch of viewer-refine also gives a live check. Consequence: the operator relies on a handoff that says the exact final argv was proven live, when the final --settings (with the Write deny) has not been run in a claude --bg session. A CLI-side surprise with the new rule would show up only at the first viewer-refine skills launch.

findings.message: Resolved (round 1 P1, a symlinked SKILL.md refused). workflow/skills.py:77-80 now checks only `exists()` and `is_file()`, both of which follow the link; the `is_symlink()` refusal is gone. workflow/test_skills.py::SkillsModuleTests.test_resolve_follows_a_skill_md_symlinked_to_a_regular_file_inside_the_folder links SKILL.md -> real.md inside the folder. It asserts that resolve_skill and check_skill pass and that copy_skill writes a real file (not a symlink) with the target's content. test_check_refuses_a_skill_md_symlinked_outside_the_folder shows that a SKILL.md linked outside the folder resolves and is then refused by the escape rule (_walk, skills.py:103-105). The task delegates refusals to PRD 4.5 ("Refusals (PRD 4.5) happen before anything is written"), and the RUNBOOK lists "a symlink that resolves outside the skill folder" among the refusals, so this does not contradict "symlinks followed". Consequence: none remaining.

The skills lane's launch argv is not asserted in full. Requirement (Acceptance 1): "the launch argv of both lanes is asserted in full (the plain lane identical to today's, the skills lane with the three flag changes and `Skill` in the tools)". workflow/test_interactive.py::InteractiveTests.test_a_skills_lane_drops_safe_mode_and_a_plain_lane_launches_byte_for_byte_as_today compares a full list only for the plain `adapter` lane (lines 531-534). For `ui` it checks piecewise (lines 521-529): `--safe-mode` absent, a 4-slot window from `--setting-sources`, the `--tools` value, and two settings keys. It never checks `--bg`, `--name`, `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config`, `--permission-mode` or the trailing prompt, and never checks that the settings JSON equals worker_settings(..., skills_lane="ui", advisor_model="fable"). test_a_repair_session_of_a_skills_lane_gets_the_same_flags is piecewise the same way and does not assert the plugin denies. The current code builds them correctly (interactive.py:349-356, 386-390), but a stray, dropped or reordered flag elsewhere in a skills argv would pass. The same gap leaves the Goal line "Everything else of the launch (deny list, `--strict-mcp-config`, pinned model and effort, permissions, launch name, prompt, receipt) is unchanged" proved only in part for the skills lane. Consequence: a future change that alters the rest of a skills lane's launch (for example, drops `--strict-mcp-config` and so lets user MCP servers in) passes the suite, and viewer-refine's UI lanes get a launch the operator did not approve.
findings.requirement: the launch argv of both lanes is asserted in full (the plain lane identical to today's, the skills lane with the three flag changes and `Skill` in the tools)

findings.message: [L1](c) preflight flags: no test shows that preflight fails without them. [L1](c): "Preflight checks that `claude --help` lists `--setting-sources` and `--plugin-dir` as it checks `--safe-mode` and `--tools`". The code adds both flags to required_flags (pipeline.py:1483). workflow/test_portable.py::PreflightClaudeFlags.test_preflight_refuses_a_claude_cli_without_settings_or_effort (lines 239-241) puts both new flags into all three stub `--help` outputs and drops only `--settings` or `--effort`. No case asserts a non-zero exit when `--setting-sources` or `--plugin-dir` is missing. The worker discloses this in `untested`: "no unit test asserts preflight fails without them". Proof on the candidate: self-report plus code. Consequence: if the two flags fell out of required_flags, a host whose CLI lacks them would pass preflight, and every skills-lane launch would then fail after prepare had written the run.

findings.message: No test covers launch forwarding a lane's skills to prepare, or refusing a skill at launch level. launch_commands appends `--lane-skills <lane>=a,b` to the prepare argv (launch.py:458-459), and it refuses an unresolvable or invalid skill before any Git action (launch.py:455-457; the RUNBOOK says "`launch` and `launch --dry-run` resolve and check the skills before any Git action"; PRD 3 says "`launch --dry-run` and `prepare` refuse a name that does not resolve, naming it"). No test asserts either. test_the_dry_run_prints_a_lanes_skills_and_the_advisor reads printed["skills"], which comes straight from lane_skills(manifest) at launch.py:653, not from the prepare command. RecordTests call prepare with `--lane-skills` by hand. test_a_2_8_0_feature_keeps_every_gate_a_2_6_0_feature_has writes no skills. The only launch-level refusal tested is the version gate (test_skills_need_version_2_8_0). The new `start --lane-skills` "prepare only" refusal (pipeline.py:1441-1446) is also untested. Consequence: if the forwarding broke, a 2.8.0 feature with `skills` would prepare and launch every lane as a plain `--safe-mode` lane with no error, and viewer-refine's UI lanes would run without impeccable. The suite would stay green.
findings.requirement: Refusals (PRD 4.5) happen before anything is written and name the lane and the skill.

findings.message: Acceptance 4 is only partly proved at prepare level. Requirement: "Each refusal of PRD 4.5 with its message, nothing written." workflow/test_pipeline.py::RecordTests.test_each_skills_refusal_before_the_run_directory_exists (lines 1661-1665) covers a missing skill, a hooks frontmatter, a 2 MB file, a bad name and a duplicate, and asserts that no run directory exists. Two PRD 4.5 refusals, "a skill folder over 8 MB in total" and "a `SKILL.md` that is not a regular file", have only module-level message tests (test_skills.py::test_check_refuses_an_oversized_file_and_an_oversized_folder, test_resolve_refuses_a_missing_or_irregular_skill_md_naming_the_lane_and_skill). For those two, "nothing written" is inferred from where the code calls check_skill. The RUNBOOK's refusal of a symlink that "forms a loop" (skills.py:96-97) has no test anywhere. Consequence: a regression that moved one of these checks after the run directory, or broke loop detection (copy_skill would then recurse until the 8 MB cap or an OSError), would not be caught.
findings.requirement: Each refusal of PRD 4.5 with its message, nothing written.

findings.message: No test covers the judges' launch in a run that has a skills lane. Requirement: "Judges (reviewers, challenge, sidecar, attack, panel) stay in safe mode and keep today's settings bytes." [L1](a) also requires that `panel_settings` and the attack pass keep today's bytes. Their code is unchanged (interactive.py:431, attack.py:334, automatic.py:1643, panel.py:649 still pass `--safe-mode`), but no test in the suite asserts `--safe-mode` on a reviewer, challenge, sidecar, attack or panel argv. No test launches a judge from a plan whose lane has `skills` to show that the judge gets neither `--setting-sources`, `--plugin-dir`, `Skill` nor the skills settings variant. Proof on the candidate: the worker's self-report ("panel.py/attack.py bytes untouched") and unchanged code. Consequence: a later change that routed judges through worker_launch_flags, or keyed it on the run instead of the lane, would give judges the operator-customizations-free but skill-loading launch [G6] rules out, and nothing would fail.
findings.requirement: Judges (reviewers, challenge, sidecar, attack, panel) stay in safe mode and keep today's settings bytes.

findings.message: No Python test covers a lane model/effort pin on a 2.8.0 feature. [L1](e) adds 2.8.0 to LANE_ROLE_VERSIONS (launch.py:43). test_a_2_7_0_lane_pin_reaches_prepare_for_its_selected_lane_only uses only 2.7.0, and test_a_2_8_0_feature_keeps_every_gate_a_2_6_0_feature_has writes no lane model/effort. Only the TS contract test parses `pinned` at 2.8.0 (contract.test.ts), and that test checks the schema, not load_feature/launch_commands. A 2.8.0 feature with both `skills` and `model`/`effort` on lanes, as in PRD section 3's example, is never loaded or launched by the workflow suite. Consequence: if 2.8.0 dropped out of LANE_ROLE_VERSIONS, viewer-refine's lanes with their own model or effort would be refused at launch ("needs version 2.7.0") and no test would catch it first.
findings.requirement: A 2.7.0 feature with `skills` is refused; a test that every 2.7.0 feature still launches unchanged after 2.8.0 joins the gate sets.
